segments.say: Lesson 6. Transformers & Self-Attention. Q, K, V, multi-head attention and the autoregressive loop, explained visually.

Self-attention lets every token in a sentence look at every other token and decide which ones matter for its meaning. It's the core idea of the transformer, the architecture inside every modern L L M. Here is an analogy. Reading "The animal didn't cross the street because it was tired", your brain links "it" to "animal" instantly. Attention is the mechanism that lets the model make that link.

Why does this matter? Explains why long context is expensive and why the K V cache matters for latency. A favourite "explain how L L Ms work" interview question. A few key words. Transformer: The neural network design built from attention plus feed-forward layers. Query / Key / Value: What a token looks for / offers / passes on. Multi-head: Several attention patterns running in parallel. Autoregressive: Generates one token at a time, feeding outputs back in. K V cache: Stored keys/values so past tokens aren't recomputed.

segments.say: Self-attention: what does "it" refer to. Sentence: "The animal didn't cross the street because it was tired." To understand "it", the model must look at the other tokens.

segments.sec: Watch: Self-attention: what does "it" refer to?
segments.say: For token "it" the model builds a Query (Q): "what am I looking for?". Every token also has a Key (K), "what do I contain?", and a Value (V), "what do I pass on?"

segments.sec: Watch: Self-attention: what does "it" refer to?
segments.say: Score equals Q("it"), K(each token). Softmax turns the scores into weights that sum to 1.

segments.sec: Watch: Self-attention: what does "it" refer to?
segments.say: "animal" gets weight 0.70 and "street" only 0.10. The model "attends" mostly to animal.

segments.sec: Watch: Self-attention: what does "it" refer to?
segments.say: New representation of "it" equals weighted sum of all the Values. Now "it" carries the meaning of "animal".

segments.sec: Watch: Self-attention: what does "it" refer to?
segments.say: This happens for every token in parallel, in many "heads" (multi-head: one tracks grammar, one coreference. ) and across dozens of layers.
The generation loop. Input tokens: "The sky is".
Each token becomes an embedding plus positional information, because attention alone doesn't know word order.
It flows through N stacked blocks, each one self-attention (mix information across tokens) then a feed-forward network (process each token).
The last position's vector is projected onto the whole vocabulary, and softmax gives a probability for every possible next token.
One token is sampled (temperature, top-p. ). Here: " blue".
It's appended and the loop repeats: autoregressive generation, one token per step until E O S or max tokens. The K V cache stores past keys and values so old tokens aren't recomputed.

Why transformers won. R N Ns read text one word at a time, which is slow and forgets long-range context. Transformers use self-attention so every token can look at every other token in parallel. That made training on massive G P U clusters practical.

Q, K, V in one breath. Each token's vector is multiplied by three learned matrices to get Q, K and V. Attention equals softmax(Q Kᵀ / √d), V. The √d scaling keeps the softmax from saturating. A causal mask stops a token from looking at future tokens during generation.

Architectures. Decoder-only (G P T, Claude, Llama): next-token generation, the basis of chat L L Ms. Encoder-only (B E R T): reads both directions, used for classification, embeddings and rerankers. Encoder-decoder (T5, original Transformer): translation and summarization.

Practical consequences. Attention cost grows roughly quadratically with sequence length, which is why long context is expensive. The K V cache makes decoding fast but eats G P U memory, and that limits concurrency in serving. "Lost in the middle": models attend best to the start and end of long contexts, so put key info there.
Analogy. A room of people (tokens). Each person shouts a question (Q). Everyone holds up a name tag (K). You listen most to people whose tag matches your question and take their information (V).

Say it in the interview. "A decoder-only transformer embeds tokens with positional info and passes them through stacked self-attention and feed-forward layers. Attention lets each token weigh every other token via Q, K similarity and mix their values. Generation is autoregressive with a K V cache, which is why latency splits into prefill and per-token decode.".

Model families. Decoder-only: left context (causal), chat, generation, agents, G P T, Claude, Llama, Mistral. Encoder-only: both directions, embeddings, classification, rerankers, B E R T, RoBERTa, cross-encoders. Encoder-decoder: input fully, output causal, translation, summarization, T5, B A R T.

A likely interview question: Explain self-attention in 30 seconds. A strong answer: Each token creates a query and compares it with every token's key. Softmax gives weights, and the token's new vector is the weighted sum of the values. That's how context like coreference gets resolved, in parallel across heads and layers.
That's it for Transformers & Self-Attention. Now play the quiz and games in the app to lock it in. See you in the next lesson.
